name: reflexion_lesson_memory
hypothesis: LLM-generated error lessons ('when facts show X the correct charge is Y, not Z') stored at learn time and injected into the prediction prompt outperform raw example storage, because the model receives pre-digested legal distinctions rather than having to infer the distinguishing rule from surface-similar examples at predict time.

name: cjk_bigram_confusion_memory
hypothesis: The base system's ASCII-only tokenizer returns near-zero Jaccard similarity for all Chinese document pairs, making retrieval random; replacing it with CJK character bigrams produces discriminative similarity scores and improves few-shot selection, while adding an explicit canonical-label anchor in the prompt reduces format-mismatch errors (~40% of score failures).

name: contrastive_error_pair_memory
hypothesis: Storing raw wrong-prediction records (predicted label, correct label, case excerpt) and retrieving the most similar past mistakes at predict time will outperform LLM-generated lesson storage, because the model receives a structurally distinct WRONG/CORRECT signal from a directly parallel case rather than an abstract rule that may mis-generalize; this specifically targets the wrong-variant errors (e.g. 盗窃 vs 破坏电力设备, 受贿 vs 非国家工作人员受贿) that persist after iteration 1.

name: cooccurrence_scaffold_memory
hypothesis: Building an explicit charge co-occurrence graph from all training ground-truth label sets and injecting a companion-charge scaffold at predict time will reduce multi-charge under-prediction (the dominant remaining failure at ~30% of errors), because it gives the model a statistically grounded list of charges to verify against the case facts rather than requiring it to spontaneously enumerate secondary charges from examples alone.
